Eve (customer): Hey team — hitting an odd auth loop after enabling device trust + SSO. Users sign in with SSO, complete MFA, then immediately start getting 401s and a page that forces re-auth. Happens across Chrome and Safari. Seen since ~9:30am PDT.

Jamie (Support): Sorry you're seeing this, Eve — can you paste the exact error the app shows? Any token error from the client?

Eve (customer): UI shows 'Session expired, please sign in' after a few seconds. In browser console we see fetch to /v1/generate returning 401 with body: `{\n  \"error\": \"invalid_session\",\n  \"message\": \"session cookie not valid\"\n}`.

Jamie (Support): Thanks. A couple quick checks: 1) did you recently rotate SSO or identity provider keys? 2) are you using the hosted redirect (app.redwood-hosted.example) or a custom domain?

Eve (customer): No key rotation on our side. We are on a custom domain edge.example.com (CNAME to Redwood proxy). I can repro with a clean browser profile.

Morgan (SRE): Pinging infra, I want the Set-Cookie headers from the SSO flow. Eve, can you run `curl -i -L -v 'https://edge.example.com/auth/callback?code=xxx'` (with a sanitized code) and paste response headers? Looking for `Set-Cookie` and any `cache-control` coming from CDN.

Eve (customer): Pasted output (sanitized):
```
< HTTP/1.1 302 Found
< Set-Cookie: session=eyJhbGciOi...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=3600; Domain=.example.com
< Set-Cookie: device_trust=1; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=31536000; Domain=.example.com
< Location: https://app.example.com/return
< Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
```

Eve (customer): After redirect to app, the browser still sends the session cookie but token validation fails server-side and the /auth/refresh endpoint returns 400 `invalid_grant`.

Priya (Auth Eng): Two quick hypotheses: 1) CDN or edge caching is returning a cached 302 that contains Set-Cookie from a previous tenant (bad). 2) Cookie encryption keys on auth service were rotated and older cookies can't be decrypted (would cause invalid_grant on refresh).

Jamie (Support): Morgan, can you grep edge logs for the request id? Eve, do you have a request-id header captured?

Eve (customer): I have `x-request-id: r-5c8a7b` in the failing requests.

Morgan (SRE): Found entries for r-5c8a7b on the proxy node. The upstream auth response shows `x-cache: HIT` from our CDN and `age: 18`. That lines up with Priya's CDN-cache hypothesis — if the CDN accidentally cached Set-Cookie responses, a session issued for user A could be replayed to user B.

Priya (Auth Eng): Oof. Our cache policy should mark `Set-Cookie` responses as `no-cache`. Looking at the edge config, `/auth/callback` was misconfigured with `cache: public` for that customer route due to an override when we added the device-trust experiment.

Jamie (Support): Eve — can you confirm whether clearing cache (hard reload or devtools -> disable cache) makes the issue go away for you immediately?

Eve (customer): Doing now... ok after hard reload and clearing the CDN edge cache via our provider UI, I can sign in and the session persists. ✅

Jamie (Support): Great — temporary mitigation: clear browser cache + purge CDN edge for the customer's domain. We'll follow up with permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

Morgan (SRE): Action items: 1) Roll back the cache override for device-trust experiment on edge routes (will push in 10m). 2) Add automated test to ensure `Set-Cookie` responses have `Cache-Control: no-store` and are not cached by CDN. 3) Audit other customer routes for similar overrides.

Priya (Auth Eng): Also will add server-side detection: if refresh returns `invalid_grant` immediately after a new Set-Cookie, log and surface to SRE with `x-auth-cookie-version` so we can differentiate key-rotation vs cache-replay.

Auth-Bot: deploy started by morgan — infra/edge: rollback-cache-experiment (deploy id: d-9482).

Jamie (Support): Eve, we marked this as high priority incident for you. We'll monitor for 24h and follow up once the rollback and tests are in. Anything else we should know (different tenant users, mobile app, API keys)?

Eve (customer): Mobile app uses same domain and it was affected too. The purge fixed mobile auth as well. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Morgan (SRE): Deploy complete. Verified `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/auth/callback` for edge.example.com. Running a scan for other routes with `Set-Cookie` and public cache headers — will report back.

Priya (Auth Eng): I'll follow up about adding an `x-auth-cookie-version` header in Set-Cookie telemetry so we can trace cookie issuance across rotations.

Jamie (Support): Leaving this thread open until monitoring shows no regressions. Thanks everyone :bows:
